sections.h2: Pricing and routes for a Sun Prairie sale
sections.html:
Three paths lead to a closing: an agent listing, a sale you run yourself, or a cash offer for the house as it stands. With a Census median home value of $365,700, Sun Prairie can show a wide gap between a full listing price and a discounted cash price, so run the math on each path before you commit.

A listing fits a move-in-ready house when you can handle showings. A cash sale is built for cases where time or condition outweighs top dollar: an inherited house, a vacant property, deferred repairs, or a move that cannot wait on a buyer's financing.

  • Compare the net after agent fees, repairs, concessions and carrying costs.
  • State in the written offer who pays the transfer fee and recording.
  • Get a closing date in writing before you commit.

Sun Prairie is the largest suburb of Madison, in eastern Dane County, and it has grown fast. The 2025 population estimate of 39,227 is 9.0 percent above the 2020 base. Many residents drive to Madison, and the mean commute is 22 minutes. A city-wide median hides a wide range, so a recent comparable sale on your own street tells you more than any single figure.

sections.h2: Does water or flooding affect Sun Prairie houses?
sections.html:
Occasional flooding happens here. The city sits in drumlin and marsh country in eastern Dane County, with hydric soils and Koshkonong Creek nearby, and spring melt adds to the load. One heavy overnight rain in April 2008 outran the storm drains and flooded residential basements.

If your basement has ever taken on water, say so on the condition report, and keep records of any sump pump, drain tile or waterproofing. Drain tile and basement drainage systems are on the city's building permit list, so confirm that the work was permitted.

Sun Prairie issues single-source building permits through its OpenGov portal, so one permit covers building, electrical, plumbing and heating on the same project. Your seller file should show a closed permit for each of these jobs.

  • Roof, siding, fascia and soffit, windows and doors.
  • Furnace, central air, water heater and water softener.
  • Decks, fences, sheds, pools and finished basements.
  • Kitchen and bathroom remodels, plus any electrical, heating or plumbing work.

Flooring, painting, cabinet swaps without plumbing or electrical, and replacing deck boards need no permit. Skipping a permit that was required can double the fee and add a daily fine. Only a passed final inspection closes a permit, so call Building Inspection at 608-825-1184 about anything left open.

The property maintenance code applies to owner-occupied homes as well as rentals. Grass and weeds must stay at 8 inches or lower, and sidewalk snow must be cleared within 24 hours after a storm ends. Resolve any open notice before you list.

Building Inspection also handles tenant complaints. When a tenant reports a maintenance problem and the owner has not responded, inspectors can visit and send an Official Notice with a deadline to correct it. A landlord may not retaliate against a tenant for reporting a violation.

The office is at 300 E. Main Street and is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Clear any open notice on a rental before you accept an offer, because a buyer's inspector will ask about it.

sections.h2: Condition report and transfer fee in Dane County
sections.html:
The owner of a home with up to four units must give the buyer a finished condition report within 10 days of contract acceptance, as Chapter 709 directs. Deliver it late and the buyer may rescind during the 2 business days after the 10 days end. Estate representatives, trustees, conservators and court-appointed fiduciaries who never lived there are excused.

Sellers also pay the state transfer fee, 30 cents per $100 of value, under section 77.22. Of the money collected, the county keeps 20 percent and the state gets the rest.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Dane County
sections.html:
The Dane County Register of Deeds records a deed for a $30 fee per document. The deed must name the grantor and grantee, carry the grantor's notarized original signature, include a legal description and show the parcel number from the tax bill.

An electronic transfer return receipt has to come with it. The transfer and recording fees can go on a single check payable to the Register of Deeds. A title company usually handles all of this, but if you are filing yourself, check each item on that list before the document leaves your hands.

sections.h2: What happens between offer and closing?
sections.html:
Start the condition report the day you accept an offer, because the 10-day period is short. Gather permit records, the parcel number from your tax bill, and any water-repair receipts. If the buyer is financing, the lender's appraisal and underwriting set the pace. A cash buyer skips both and buys as-is, pricing any damage into the offer.

At the closing you sign the deed, the electronic return is filed, and the register records the deed. Your payoff, the prorated property tax and the transfer fee all appear on the settlement statement, so read it before you sign.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Dane County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30 per document. The state transfer fee is separate, at 30 cents per $100 of value, and both can be paid with one check. An electronic transfer return receipt must accompany the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit history before selling my Sun Prairie home?
faqs.a: Buyers and inspectors ask for it. Sun Prairie issues permits through its OpenGov portal, and Building Inspection at 608-825-1184 can tell you if a permit is still open. Closing open permits before listing keeps the sale on schedule.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the 10-day condition report deadline?
faqs.a: The buyer may rescind the contract by written notice within 2 business days after the 10-day period ends and is entitled to the return of any deposits. Deliver the completed report early so that right never arises.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Sun Prairie that has water damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Answer the condition report's questions about water honestly and keep records of any sump pump, drain tile or waterproofing work. A cash buyer purchases as-is and prices the damage in.

faqs.q: Are there rules about parking an RV at my Sun Prairie house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city allows seasonal storage of oversized recreational vehicles from April 1 to November 30 on a paved surface with setbacks and current tags, limited to one oversized vehicle at a time. Neighborhood covenants can be stricter and the city does not enforce them.
